correctness.rationale: For every admissible state in binade k, \(a<u_E\le u_k\) prevents intermediate binade crossing and exact \(p+r\) truncation yields \(s+v_k\lfloor a/v_k\rfloor\). Thus the increment probability \(q_k\) is independent of the state within k, positive for \(k<L\), and exactly zero at terminal \(s=2^L\). There are precisely \(2^{p-1}\) increments per binade. Independence of fresh Bernoulli trials yields independent geometric waiting times and the NB convolution; moments and generating functions follow. Ideal SR always has \(a/u_k>0\), and countably many almost-sure successes imply unbounded growth. Exact-rational standalone verifier passed 62,496 states but cannot prove the infinite-time claim.

originality.rationale: The 2024 and 2026 primary full texts establish the truncation-based SR model and finite-\(n\) perturbation analysis, and the 2025 hardware study explicitly shows guard-bit absorption. All of these premises and the bare possibility of lost updates are excluded from the claimed novelty. The new exact parametric absorption-time PGF, moment classification, bounded binade count, and ideal-versus-limited almost-sure contrast were not found in the directly inspected source texts, the cited nearby prior work, targeted web searches or published-finding corpus. This is a bounded best-knowledge judgment, not proof of unique discovery.
residual_risks: An indexed or unindexed prior work might already compute this specialized Markov law under a different name.
Absorption for addends lost below the guard-grid is a known qualitative phenomenon; originality attaches only to the full explicit barrier/time distribution.
Other few-bit stochastic rounders have different behavior and may eliminate this mechanism; the theorem is intentionally operator-specific.

value.rationale: The model is directly motivated by the limited-guard-bit resource/accuracy tradeoff in current numerical arithmetic. Quantifying the exact stopping-time distribution, moments and the at-most-\(r\)-binade saturation barrier gives a reproducible long-horizon reliability benchmark where finite-\(n\) error analyses are inadequate; the complete operator-conditional classification is mathematically more informative than a trivial one-step truncation observation. Its narrow scope is natural (constant increments are the cleanest persistent update test) and identifies a relevant failure mode that sticky-bit hardware mitigations specifically target.
